title: An interrupt between the creation of a landing ticket and the assignment of its name leaves the ticket in the queue, and the landing lock's SIGTERM handler is not restored
goal: landing_lock removes a ticket it created on any interrupt, also one that lands between os.open and the assignment of the ticket name; landing_lock restores the SIGTERM handler it replaced, on a normal exit and on an interrupt in the same window

run:
import os, subprocess, sys, tempfile
sys.path.insert(0, "_tools")
import bl_close
t = tempfile.mkdtemp()
subprocess.run(["git", "init", "-q", t], check=True)
qdir = bl_close.landing_queue_dir(bl_close.landing_lock_path(t))
real = os.fdopen
def boom(*a, **k):
    os.fdopen = real
    raise KeyboardInterrupt
os.fdopen = boom  # an interrupt lands between the creation of the ticket and the assignment of its name
try:
    with bl_close.landing_lock(t, "ST-aaaaaaaa"):
        pass
except BaseException as e:
    print("interrupted by", type(e).__name__)
finally:
    os.fdopen = real
left = os.listdir(qdir) if qdir.is_dir() else []
print("tickets left in the queue:", left)
sys.exit(0 if not left else 1)

import os, signal, subprocess, sys, tempfile
sys.path.insert(0, "_tools")
import bl_close
t = tempfile.mkdtemp()
subprocess.run(["git", "init", "-q", t], check=True)
def mine(*_):
    pass
signal.signal(signal.SIGTERM, mine)
with bl_close.landing_lock(t, "ST-aaaaaaaa"):
    pass
normal = signal.getsignal(signal.SIGTERM) is mine
real = os.fdopen
def boom(*a, **k):
    os.fdopen = real
    raise KeyboardInterrupt
os.fdopen = boom
try:
    with bl_close.landing_lock(t, "ST-aaaaaaaa"):
        pass
except BaseException:
    pass
finally:
    os.fdopen = real
interrupted = signal.getsignal(signal.SIGTERM) is mine
print("handler restored after a normal exit:", normal, "after an interrupt:", interrupted)
sys.exit(0 if normal and interrupted else 1)

clauses.clause: landing_lock removes a ticket it created on any interrupt, also one that lands between os.open and the assignment of the ticket name
landing_lock restores the SIGTERM handler it replaced, on a normal exit and on an interrupt in the same window

gates.question: How does landing_lock make sure an interrupt after os.open leaves no ticket, and what does it do with a ticket whose file cannot be written?
options: Hold the ticket name before the file is made, one try/finally covers the ticket and the SIGTERM handler, a ticket whose write fails is removed
Keep the name assigned after os.open and only widen the except to BaseException
gates.recommendation: Hold the ticket name before the file is made, one try/finally covers the ticket and the SIGTERM handler, a ticket whose write fails is removed
gates.answer: Hold the ticket name before the file is made, one try/finally covers the ticket and the SIGTERM handler, a ticket whose write fails is removed
